A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods and benchmark groups, and their text and visual material support comparison. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes Appendices A–F.

before.justification: Tables 1–11 report original detector evaluations, ablations, efficiency measurements, and calibration results across six benchmark groups.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and includes additional classwise results, SD-3-M evaluations, confusion matrices, and qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: The proposed feature extraction, multi-timestep fusion, feature/object alignment, and optimization objectives remain unchanged. Appendix B elaborates existing components; the SD-3-M experiment does not document a revised algorithm or adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six benchmark groups and associated domains, categories, weather conditions, and corruptions. The appendix adds analyses and model configurations on existing coverage, without introducing a new dataset or detection scenario.

E2.justification: The appendix substantially expands comparisons within retained tasks: Table 12 adds DA-Faster and STABR on Comic; Table 13 adds UMT, IIOD, SADA, CDG, and VDD on Watercolor; Table 14 adds IBN-Net, SW, IterNorm, and ISW on Diverse Weather. Existing main-table comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 16 adds an SD-3-M model configuration, Appendix E introduces UMAP and confusion-matrix diagnostics, and Figure 15 identifies an FR-R50 baseline for corruption examples. Existing training budgets, metrics, diffusion settings, and loss weights remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and calibration analysis, v2 adds diffusion-version sensitivity analysis, domain-distribution visualizations, confusion-matrix error analyses on FoggyCityscapes and Clipart, and detection case studies across the benchmark suite. These provide substantial new diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained reliability diagrams concern predictive calibration and do not constitute newly added experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main-table results are retained, but Tables 12–16 add extensive classwise entries and SD-3-M results, including 59.1 on RainyCityscapes and 28.7 on Clipart. New qualitative findings accompany these results. Some appendix entries conflict with retained results: SD-2.1 guided Night-Rainy mAP is 20.8 in Table 14 versus 20.0 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1–7 retain their mathematical content. Despite the supplement overview mentioning derivations, Appendix B supplies explanatory motivation rather than new definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: diffusion features for generalized detection and efficient transfer through feature/object alignment. The headline 14.0% and 15.9% mAP improvement claims and six-benchmark scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendices D–E introduce architectural explanations for SD-3-M's weaker transfer and interpret confusion matrices as showing reduced missed detections. Appendix C further attributes difficult artistic transfer to feature-alignment challenges. These substantially broaden the explanatory discussion beyond the retained efficiency and extreme-domain-shift limitations.

D1.justification: v2 removes Section 4.2's explicit statement that code and trained models are supplied in supplementary materials. The abstract retains the identical code link, and existing implementation settings remain unchanged. This changes the resource disclosure without establishing that any resources were actually withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting appendix comparators and analyses, including normalization methods, UMAP, and U-Net, and replaces the Fast R-CNN reference with Faster R-CNN. The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence are largely retained, with contact-detail edits, small paragraph rearrangements, and removed supplementary-material pointers. The new supplement adds an organized overview and expanded explanations without extensively rewriting the main narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12–16 and Figures 7–15, including classwise tables, distribution plots, confusion matrices, and extensive prediction panels. Existing displays are also rearranged: calibration Table 11/Figure 6 become Table 10/Figure 5, while the component-ablation table and loss-weight figure are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added classwise results, error diagnostics, and SD-3-M comparison make the empirical evidence more inspectable and clarify architectural limits. However, appendix Table 14 conflicts with main Table 5, and Appendix D overstates SD-1.5's superiority despite SD-3-M leading on RainyCityscapes in Table 16. These reporting problems limit the net benefit of an otherwise useful supplementary expansion.
